Context:
**Project overview of Auto Task via Google Meeting (Salesforce DX), with risks found**

This was a read-only review of the whole project. No code was changed. The app connects each user to Google, and a scheduled job then works through each active Meeting_Configuration__c in turn. For each one it pulls the Gemini meeting notes from Google Drive (Google Docs whose names start with '<Config Name> -'), reads the 'Suggested next steps' section and creates Meeting_Task__c records with status 'Pending Reviewed'. When a task is approved, a record-triggered flow creates a standard Task. The review found a deployment blocker and a silent-failure bug, listed under open issues.

**Open issues**
- MeetingTaskBatch calls MeetingTaskHelper.getAssigneeIdByNameMatch, but no MeetingTaskHelper class exists in force-app. Deploying from this repo will fail unless the class already exists in the target org. Get it from the org or write it.
- If GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken() returns a blank token, MeetingNotesQueueable.execute returns without calling moveToNext(). The job chain stops, so every configuration after the failing one is skipped for that run. That return also comes before `insert logs`, so the 'Authentication token is blank.' Meeting_Log__c is never saved and the failure leaves no record.
- Tokens come from the running user's User record (GoogleAuth.getValidAccessToken). The scheduled job therefore uses the Google account of whoever scheduled it, not the account of each configuration's owner.
- objects/User/ has about 90 field files from managed packages (Pardot, Maps, SBQQ, et4ae5 and others). Only the four Google_* fields belong to this project. Deploying the whole folder may conflict with those packages, so consider trimming it.
- There are no Apex test classes or LWC Jest tests in the repo, so the code can't reach the test coverage Salesforce requires to deploy to production.
- Video_Meeting__c appears to be an older data model that the main notes-to-tasks process doesn't use. It is a candidate for removal once that is confirmed.
- The project folder is not a git repository yet.

**Enterprise-readiness assessment of Auto Task via Google Meeting, which found a token leak to the browser**

The user asked whether the project is ready for enterprise use. The verdict was no: it is a single-org proof of concept. Rechecking the code found a new critical security issue: every connected user's Google access token is sent to the browser. It also confirmed that tokens and the OAuth client secret are stored in plain text. No code was changed. Claude offered to fix the token leak, and the user has not replied yet.

**Open issues**
- CRITICAL: the user-filter method in GoogleGeminiService (about line 105) runs SELECT Id, Name, Google_Access_Token__c FROM User and returns those User records through an @AuraEnabled UserFilterWrapper.users. Any user who can open the LWC can read every connected colleague's live Google token in browser dev tools, and that token can read their Drive. Fix: remove the token from the query (use the token only for a server-side filter, or a separate IsNotBlank check) or return a DTO with only Id and Name. Fix this before any further rollout.
- The Google_Access_Token__c and Google_Refresh_Token__c fields on User are unencrypted LongTextArea fields. Meeting_PS gives read and edit access to both, and Video_Meeting_PS also grants permissions on them, so admins and permission-set holders can see the tokens.
- The Google_Token__mdt object, which holds Client_Secret__c (a plain Text field), has Public visibility, so the OAuth client secret is not protected. This adds to the case for the proposed (not yet agreed) move to an External Credential with per-user principals plus a Named Credential.
- Other enterprise gaps: an AppExchange security review is needed if the app will be sold; the Drive-wide OAuth scope usually needs approval from the customer's Google Workspace admin; and token revocation, callout limits and scaling to many configurations are not handled.

**Decisions**
- MeetingTaskHelper.getAssigneeIdByNameMatch matches the user's first name only, because MeetingTaskBatch queries only FirstName. Meeting attendees are checked first; if several are named, the one mentioned earliest wins, since Gemini puts the owner first (e.g. '[Name] do X'). If no attendee matches, it falls back to all active users, but only accepts a first name exactly one active user has. Matches are whole-word and ignore case ('Ann' does not match 'Annual'). If nothing matches safely it returns null and the task is created unassigned rather than given to the wrong person.
- Tests create no users and run as the current user, changing only the Google_* fields on that user. Reason: managed-package (FSSK) validation rules on User could block inserting test users.
- The GoogleAuth tests read the real Google_Token__mdt record, because Apex tests cannot create custom metadata records.
- The queueable tests call MeetingNotesQueueable.execute(null) directly instead of enqueueing it. Test.setCreatedDate fixes the order of configurations, so each chain is only one level deep. This avoids Salesforce's ban on chaining queueable jobs in tests.
- Tests do not assert on Meeting_Log__c rows from the queueable's early-return paths (see open issues), so the tests do not treat that bug as correct behaviour.

It is the Apex controller for the activity calendar LWCs (bffSchFullCalendarV7, bffSchCalendarFilterbar, legacy activityCalendarV7). - No code decisions were made; this was a read-only review.
- rescheduleAppointment deliberately runs in this order. It clears IsPrimaryResource on outgoing resources (FSL refuses to delete a primary resource) and deletes them. It then updates the appointment times and inserts the incoming resources last. Otherwise the ServiceAppointment before-update trigger would check the old resource against the new time and wrongly block the move. Keep this order if you refactor.

- bookServiceAppointment is a stub that always returns success=false and 'Booking from this calendar view is not yet implemented.' It exists only so legacy activityCalendarV7 compiles. Anyone booking from that view gets this error until it is implemented or the view is retired.
- buildAssignedResources is private and has no caller in the class, so it looks like dead code.
- The ConflictDetail.conflictReason comment lists only APPOINTMENT_OVERLAP and SHIFT_COVERAGE. checkResourceAvailability also emits ABSENCE and CROSS_PROPERTY_BUFFER. Any front-end code that switches on the reason must handle all four.
- ResourceConflictResult.conflictType is declared but checkTimeConflict never sets it.
- The conflict checks do not use one common rule for which appointment statuses count as cancelled. Some use the BFF_SCH_Constants.SERVICEAPPOINTMENT_CANCELLED_STATUSES list. Others hardcode 'Canceled'. getAvailableAlternatives does not filter cancelled appointments when finding busy resources.
- Shift matching depends on BFF_SCH_ShiftRecurrenceUtil, which works in Eastern-time dates. Any change to recurring-shift behaviour must also be made in the several parallel queries in this class (getApp..., checkResourceAvailability, validateResourcesForUpdate, getAvailableAlternatives, and the prep/cleanup checks).

- The Additional Staff busy query (resolveBusyStaffResourceIds) does not filter AssignedResource by candidate ids, so it scans all overlapping assignments in the window. This could be slow or hit limits in a busy org.

**Why bffSchActivityCalendar calls Apex imperatively instead of with @wire, plus a missing-parameter bug found**

The user asked why the bffSchActivityCalendar LWC calls Apex imperatively rather than with @wire. Each of its six Apex calls was checked against its @AuraEnabled annotation. Using imperative calls is a sound choice here: the data feeds the third-party FullCalendar library rather than the LWC template, calls are triggered by FullCalendar callbacks and user drag/resize actions, and several calls must run in a fixed order. No code was changed. One bug was found: the JS never passes serviceAppointmentId to getAvailableAlternatives.

**Decisions**
- Keep the Apex calls in bffSchActivityCalendar imperative. Do not convert them to @wire.
- rescheduleAppointment must stay imperative because it writes data, and @wire only accepts cacheable=true methods, which cannot write data.
- checkResourceAvailability, getAvailableAlternatives and getAppAndShiftForSelectedDateForGivenResource are not cacheable. They must return live data, run in response to FullCalendar callbacks (datesSet, eventDrop, eventResize), and getAvailableAlternatives runs once per conflict in order (Room → Staff → Vehicle). A wire cannot do any of that. With a wire, refreshing after a reschedule would also need refreshApex.
- getCalendarsAllMetadata and getLicenseKey are cacheable=true and could technically be wired. They stay imperative because initializeComponent needs a strict order: metadata, then the FullCalendar files, then the license key, then the calendar constructor. They still get client-side caching because they are cacheable.

**Open issues**
- Bug, not fixed: in Apex, getAvailableAlternatives takes serviceAppointmentId as its first parameter (BFF_SCH_ActivityCalendarHandler.cls line ~603). bffSchActivityCalendar.js (line ~662) never passes it, so it arrives as null. If the method uses it, for example to leave the appointment being moved out of the busy-resource check, the alternatives returned may be wrong. Check whether bffSchActivityCalendarV7 has the same gap.
- bffSchActivityCalendar.js seems to duplicate the legacy bffSchActivityCalendarV7 reschedule flow, including its silent failures: a reschedule or availability-check error only logs to the console and reverts the drag, with no toast. Fixes may be needed in both components.

**Why the meetingConfiguration LWC calls Apex imperatively instead of with @wire, plus a stale-cache risk on its auth checks**

The user asked why meetingConfiguration calls Apex imperatively rather than with @wire. Each of its seven Apex methods was checked against its @AuraEnabled annotation and its body. Imperative calls are the right choice here. Most of the methods write data, so they cannot be cacheable, and @wire only accepts cacheable methods. The flow also has to run in a fixed order. No code was changed.

**Decisions**
- Keep the Apex calls in meetingConfiguration imperative. Do not convert them to @wire.
- requestAccessToken, logoutUser and syncMeetingsToDb write data, so they cannot be cacheable=true and cannot be wired.
- GoogleCalendarService.getMyMeetings looks like a read-only call, but it cannot be cacheable either. When the Google token has expired it refreshes it and runs `update new User(...)` (GoogleCalendarService.cls lines ~108-113), and it makes a live Google callout whose results should not be cached.
- The flow must run in a fixed order: connectedCallback exchanges any OAuth ?code=, then checks isUserAuthenticated, and only then do goToStep2 and loadUserEmail/loadMeetings run. The remaining calls are triggered by button clicks or filter changes. A wire fires on its own and would race with the OAuth code exchange.

**Open issues**
- Possible stale-auth bug, not fixed: GoogleAuth.isUserAuthenticated and getAuthenticatedEmail are @AuraEnabled(cacheable=true), so even imperative calls can be answered from the browser's cache. After a logout or a reconnect, the screen may briefly show the old login status or the previous account's email. Suggested fix: make both methods non-cacheable, because auth state changes. If they stay cacheable, call refreshApex or notifyRecordUpdateAvailable after login and logout.

**meetingConfiguration LWC re-reviewed: imperative vs @wire confirmed, plus new security and config findings**

The user asked for a review of meetingConfiguration covering imperative vs @wire and any other configuration that could be improved, with no code changes. The earlier decision to keep all Apex calls imperative still holds. The review found new issues in the OAuth/token handling, error handling, js-meta.xml and LWC code quality. It also confirmed that every open issue from the 10-23 and 10-29 meetingConfiguration handoffs is still in the code. No code was changed and nothing was deployed.

**Decisions**
- Keep every meetingConfiguration Apex call imperative and do not add @wire. This re-confirms the 10-23 decision: requestAccessToken, logoutUser and syncMeetingsToDb write data, getMyMeetings makes a callout and can update User, and a wire would race with the ?code= exchange in connectedCallback.
- Recommended removing cacheable=true from GoogleAuth.isUserAuthenticated and getAuthenticatedEmail rather than wiring them, because auth state changes and cached results can show a stale login status or email after logout or reconnect. Optional: merge them into one non-cacheable getAuthState() returning {isAuthenticated, email}.
- Suggested order: (1) make the auth methods non-cacheable and fix the toast-variant and spinner bugs, (2) clean up js-meta.xml, @track and if:true, (3) treat the Named Credential/External Credential move as a separate design decision.

**Open issues**
- Security: Google access and refresh tokens are stored in plain User fields that anyone with field access can read. Consider a Named Credential plus an External Credential with per-user principals.
- The OAuth URL has no state parameter, so the callback is not protected against CSRF.
- logoutUser only clears the User fields and never revokes the Google grant (https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke).
- redirectUri points to /apex/GoogleOAuthCallback. The LWC's handleOAuthCallback (?code=) only runs if that VF page sends the user back to the LWC page with the code. Confirm which one actually exchanges the code; the LWC path may be dead code.
- The token refresh logic exists twice: GoogleAuth.refreshAndSaveToken and GoogleCalendarService.getValidTokenResponse. The second passes a blank refresh token to urlEncode(null) and throws an unclear error.
- syncMeetingsToDb doesn't check field-level security or object permissions (with sharing only covers record sharing). Use upsert as user or Security.stripInaccessible.
- getMyMeetings catches its own AuraHandledException and re-wraps it with e.getMessage(), which is 'Script-thrown exception', so the real error is lost. The LWC also ignores error.body.message and shows a generic toast.
- js-meta.xml: lightning__RecordPage is exposed although the component doesn't use recordId. masterLabel is the camelCase API name and there is no description.
- LWC code quality: @track is used on every field but none need it. if:true/if:false should become lwc:if. showFuture is always reset to true, so includeFuture is effectively unused. loadMeetings has no guard against out-of-order responses when 'Show past' is toggled quickly. The Logout control is a clickable span that the keyboard can't reach. Clean up the inline style, the console.log calls and the System.debug calls that print attendee emails.
- Still unfixed from the earlier handoffs: the error object is passed as the toast variant (js line 464), and the spinner hides before the reload after a save finishes (line 460). The remaining issues in the 10-23 and 10-29 meetingConfiguration handoffs are also still present.
